query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled titanium surface enrichment on boride-based components will improve molten-aluminum corrosion resistance by forming a stable, Ti-rich interfacial layer that acts as a diffusion barrier against aluminum attack.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components with their typical microstructure and composition as used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
generation.intervention: Apply a surface treatment (e.g., through diffusion or thin film deposition) to introduce a nanoscale, controlled layer enriched in titanium on the component surfaces.
generation.conditions: Exposure to molten aluminum at typical plating bath temperatures and cycling thermal conditions, with the treatment optimized to resist long-term high-temperature diffusion.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Ti-rich interfacial layer that may form stable compounds (e.g., TiB2 or TiO2) which remain intact during high-temperature exposure and inhibit aluminum penetration.
generation.mechanism: The Ti-enriched layer creates a protective barrier that limits interdiffusion between the boride substrate and molten aluminum, reducing corrosion rates. Similar benefits from titanium additions have been observed in related alloy systems (e.g., PMC9962455), supporting the idea that Ti can enhance corrosion resistance by stabilizing surface phases.
generation.predicted_outcome: Treated components are expected to show a measurable reduction in corrosion depth and interface degradation compared to untreated samples—potentially translating to a service life extension (for instance, an improvement on the order of 20-30% under similar conditions), although the precise magnitude remains uncertain.
generation.baseline: Standard, untreated boride-based components currently used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
generation.boundary: The protective effect is dependent on achieving an optimal Ti concentration and layer thickness; if the layer is too thin or degrades under prolonged high-temperature exposure, the benefit may diminish. Additionally, changes in plating bath chemistry or impurities may affect the stability of the Ti-rich barrier.
generation.uncertainty: Key uncertainties include the optimal processing conditions to achieve the desired Ti enrichment, the long-term stability of the protective layer under cycling thermal conditions, and the precise quantification of the corrosion improvement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of boride-based component samples: one group receives the titanium surface enrichment treatment and the other group remains untreated. Subject both groups to identical molten aluminum immersion tests under conditions representative of hot-dip aluminum-plating operations. Analyze the samples periodically to assess interfacial degradation and corrosion depth.
measurements: Ti concentration profiles across the interface
Phase identification of the protective layer (using XRD or electron microscopy)
Service life estimation under accelerated corrosion conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in corrosion depth and improved phase stability at the interface compared to the untreated controls, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

Effect of Ti on Characterization and Properties of CoCrFeNiTix High Entropy Alloy Prepared Via Electro-Deoxidization of the Metal Oxides and Vacuum Hot Pressing Sintering Process

Abstract: The CoCrFeNi system is one of the most important high entropy alloys (HEAs) systems. By adding and adjusting the alloy element components and using different synthesis methods, different phases, organization and microstructure can be obtained, thus improving their properties. In this study, CoCrFeNiTix HEAs with various Ti contents (x in molar ratio, x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) were fabricated by an electrochemical process by virtue of different oxides. The impacts of different Ti contents on the structure, distribution of elements, mechanical properties and corrosion behavior were researched using XRD, EDX and other testing methods. The bulk CoCrFeNiTix (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) HEAs could be obtained through vacuum hot pressing sintering process (VHPS), which had a single-phase FCC structure. The results of the study showed that the bulk CoCrFeNiTix exhibited superior ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and hardness, with the UTS of CoCrFeNiTi as high as 783 MPa and the hardness of CoCrFeNiTi1.5 reaching 6
